conclusion: F5 wall mechanism fully measured on NV: the fused u64 cross-tile reduce r_16_4_1187 reads its 607KB packed-keys input L2-cold after the 315us vocab GEMV epilogue, paying DRAM latency (84.7-85.7us) instead of the L2-warm 44.0us. A 2.2us warm-up copy of the keys before the reduce restores 44.0us, proving the wall is L2 residency, not kernel body, launch config, or NV-vs-CUDA. This flips the fused tail from +25.8us slower to ~-11us faster than the legacy chain.

epi_gemv_chain_copy_warm.mode: epi GEMV then 2.2us keys.clone() then reduce (like legacy E_1187_32_4)

epi_gemv_chain_direct.mode: epi GEMV writes keys then reduce reads them directly (mimics in-situ)

flush_l2_then_reduce.mode: 155 MB unrelated write flushes L2, then reduce over same warm buffer

isolated_fresh_alloc.mode: fresh Tensor.empty keys each replay, no GEMV

isolated_warm_keys.mode: reduce over L2-warm reused keys buffer

method: PROFILE=1 HCQ per-kernel GPU timestamps on NV; isolated control experiments on the same kernel
